In the paper's reported C4 perplexity and eight-task zero-shot accuracy tables, it outperforms TEAL and WINA at each tested target sparsity on Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B. These are author-reported results from a single A100 SXM4 40 GB setup, with hyperparameters selected on WikiText-2; the study reports FLOP-level savings and explicitly leaves kernel-level wall-clock performance for future work.

item.title: A SkillsBench study reports that agent-skill utility depends on model–harness fit and artifact organization
item.description: Cheng et al. report a controlled study of agent skills on 87 SkillsBench tasks across three models and three harnesses. The same benchmark-supplied skills help some configurations and hurt others on 32 tasks (36.78%). On 23 single-skill tasks, operation-support reranking raises first-choice pass rates by 4.35–5.80 points across three selected configurations; on multi-skill tasks, stage-plan and dependency-DAG organization generally outperform simple ordering. These are author-reported preprint results based on three runs per condition. The study does not measure runtime, token or maintenance costs, and independent transfer beyond the selected task and configuration sets remains unknown.

item.title: CNNIC reports more than 700 million generative-AI users in China by mid-2026
item.description: CNNIC's 2026-09-30 announcement says its report, released the previous day, estimates more than 700 million generative-AI users in China and penetration above 50% by the first half of 2026. It also reports high use of question-answering and more than 100% year-over-year growth in usage counts for assistant and office-efficiency apps. These are claims made in CNNIC's announcement: the accessible page does not provide the underlying report, survey frame, definitions, denominators or uncertainty, so the measures cannot yet be independently assessed or compared with earlier waves.

item.title: OpenAI manuscript claims the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2
item.description: OpenAI’s 23-page manuscript claims that for every ν>2 there is a threshold Q(ν) such that |π−p/q|≥q^-ν for all integers p and q≥Q(ν), and concludes that π has irrationality exponent 2. If correct, this would sharply improve the prior upper bounds discussed in the paper. The threshold is ineffective; the manuscript does not prove a uniform c/q² lower bound or bounded continued-fraction partial quotients. OpenAI’s public family-017 note describes a Lean statement covering the exponent claim, but no independent build, semantic audit or number-theory review was performed here. Treat the theorem as claimed, not established.

item.title: Japan’s energy-conservation regime adds data-centre reporting and a PUE threshold for eligible new builds
item.description: Japan’s Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ENECHO) describes additional Energy Conservation Act measures for data-centre operators, including reporting and public disclosure from FY2026 submissions and a PUE≤1.3 standard for eligible new sites from FY2029, assessed after two operating years. Its guidance lists scope thresholds and exclusions. This is an official policy design and reporting obligation; it does not show facility compliance, achieved efficiency, capacity, or AI workload costs.

item.title: Shanghai prioritizes computing facilities in its green-power direct-connection pilot plan
item.description: Shanghai’s Development and Reform Commission issued a city implementation plan for single- and multi-user direct connections between renewable generators and electricity users. The original Chinese notice prioritizes computing facilities, sets source-load matching and self-use conditions, requires grid-connected projects to pay transmission and system-operation fees, and establishes an application, evaluation and project-library process. The plan targets 500 MW of generation-side project development by 2030. A bounded official-index check did not retrieve the first selected-project library promised after the 15 Aug 2026 application deadline; project selection, data-centre economics and operating outcomes remain unknown.

item.title: A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates
item.description: Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen compare OpenAI’s natural-language Navier-Stokes proof with cited Lean declarations. In Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), they report that the paper states an m+4 derivative estimate while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5 derivatives. For equation (10.19), they report a distinct pressure-flux bound and proof route in Lean. The authors argue that these examples challenge whether the formalization faithfully verifies the announced prose. This is a source-reported analysis, not an independent refutation of the underlying blow-up theorem; it is an October 6 preprint without established peer review or specialist consensus in this check.

item.title: Mingbird reports improved artifact completion by small local models on a bounded agent benchmark
item.description: The authors compare a local-first agent harness with three stock harnesses across four small open models and 18 self-built tasks, reporting an average task score of 0.886 for Mingbird versus 0.631, 0.479 and 0.405 for the named baselines. A separate 278-task tau-squared comparison reports 0.856 under a common user simulator. The paper publishes per-cell results and discusses artifact checks, finish gates and anti-loop controls. These are author-reported benchmark results: the primary matrix uses one machine, one counted run per cell and tasks co-developed with some harness mechanisms.

item.title: China opens 2026 green-compute facility recommendations with energy, carbon, water and utilization criteria
item.description: A five-agency Chinese notice opens recommendations for 2026 national green-compute facilities. It requires at least one year of stable operation, specified energy-efficiency and green-data-center levels, renewable-electricity share at least the provincial responsibility weight, and measured energy, water and compute-utilization information; ordinary facilities generally need at least 3,000 standard racks and 60% rack occupancy, with stated exceptions. Applications are due 16 November 2026 and the agencies say they will review submissions before publishing a recommended list. These are eligibility and screening rules, not evidence of facility compliance, selection outcomes or improved AI-compute economics.
